transcript.text: microwve plate wont go round anymore, food hot on one side cold on other. still heats tho

Since it still heats, the magnetron is fine. The problem is almost always the turntable parts or the small motor underneath. Check these in order, easiest first:

1. Turntable setting
Some microwaves have a "turntable on/off" button, often used for large dishes. Make sure it hasn't been switched off by accident. Check your manual if you're unsure.

2. Plate and roller ring
• Take out the glass plate and the roller ring (the wheeled ring underneath).
• Clean both, plus the track on the microwave floor. Dried food or grease can jam them.
• Make sure the rollers spin freely and aren't cracked or missing.
• Put everything back with the plate's underside notches sitting properly on the center coupler.

3. Center coupler (drive hub)
This is the small plastic piece in the middle of the floor that the plate locks onto.
• Check that it's seated firmly on the motor shaft.
• Look for cracks or stripped/rounded edges. These wear out often.
• A replacement costs about $5–15. Search your microwave's model number (on a sticker inside the door frame or on the back) plus "turntable coupler."

4. Turntable motor
If the coupler is fine but doesn't turn (or only twitches) while the microwave runs, the motor under the floor has likely failed.
• Replacement motors are cheap ($10–25), but fitting one means removing the outer case or a bottom panel.
• Safety warning: Microwaves contain a high-voltage capacitor that can hold a dangerous charge even when unplugged. If you're not experienced with this, have a repair person do it, or weigh the cost against a new microwave.

Meanwhile: Stop the microwave halfway through, rotate and stir the food, then continue. That evens out the heating.

Most of the time it's step 2 or 3, which are easy fixes.

no turntable button on mine. roller ring is in and the wheels spin fine, nothing stuck under it. the little plastic piece in the middle has a crack in it and the hole looks rounded. plate sits on it but wobbles. model on the back is R272WM

That cracked, rounded coupler is almost certainly the problem. The motor is likely turning, but the worn hole just spins on the shaft instead of gripping it.

What to order
R272WM looks like a Sharp model. Search "Sharp R272WM turntable coupler" or "drive coupling" on appliance parts sites, Amazon, or eBay. Before buying, check that the listing names your model number, because couplers look similar but differ in height and hole shape. Expect about $5–15.

Fitting it (no tools needed)
1. Unplug the microwave.
2. Lift out the plate and roller ring.
3. Pull the old coupler straight up off the shaft. It should come off by hand.
4. Look at the metal or plastic shaft it sat on. It's usually D-shaped (round with one flat side). Make sure that flat edge isn't worn smooth.
5. Line up the new coupler's hole with the shaft's flat side and push it down firmly until it seats.
6. Replace the ring and plate, checking that the plate's underside notches sit on the coupler's arms.

Test it
Put a cup of water in and run it for 30 seconds. The plate should turn smoothly without wobbling.

If the new coupler doesn't turn
The shaft itself may be worn, or the motor has failed. In that case you'd need a turntable motor, which means opening the case. The high-voltage capacitor warning from before applies, so a repair shop is the safer route.

Until the part arrives, it's fine to keep using the microwave. Just stop halfway, rotate and stir the food, then continue.
